design_critique:
1) The revised design is identical to iteration 2 in geometry and controller (kp 3.0, ki 0.3, kd 0.4, base_speed 1.6, last_direction, sensors at x -0.06 to 0.06, y 0.06, 16 mm footprints). The contract makes each race deterministic per seed and track, so this run should reproduce iteration 2's score of 132.0028 and its per-track metrics. It adds no new evidence about any parameter. If the race is the only test this iteration, the design cannot teach the team anything.

2) The known failure remains unaddressed. In iteration 2, 19 of 20 oval trials, all 20 s-bend trials and all 20 slalom trials ended off track. max_error is pinned at about 0.06 m, the off-track limit, on every track. Progress is 0.45, 0.27 and 0.16. The design keeps the same edge behaviour, where a sensor at the outer edge saturates the signal at plus or minus 2, so turn is about kp times 2 (about 2100 PWM at kp 3.0). The rationale does not check whether that saturation causes the overshoot that exits the track.

3) Line loss persists on the s-bend (0.65 per run) and slalom (0.8 per run). Last_direction at throttle 0.35 is kept without any test of its time or progress cost on those tracks.

4) Speed is not shown to be non-binding. The oval finish at 1.88 s is one success in 20 trials, and that run is the best of the set (score 933.93). It does not establish time margin on the s-bend or slalom, which never finished.

5) The integral term (ki 0.3, clamp plus or minus 2, so up to about 0.6 turn, about 210 PWM) is retained with no isolated test. Iteration 3 changed only ki and was worse, so the direction of the ki effect is not established either way.
rationale_critique:
1) The rationale states that the expected result is 'the same distribution as iteration 2' and gives a 'one-in-twenty finish chance'. This is wrong under the contract. Seed and track fix the disturbance, so the outcome is deterministic, not a 1-in-20 draw. The race will return the same finish or non-finish, not a new sample.

2) The kd argument cites the wrong evidence. It says 'Iteration 1 (kd 0.6) had lower oscillation than iteration 2 (kd 0.4)'. The history shows no kd 0.6 race. Iteration 1 used kd 0.4 with kp 2.5 and base_speed 1.5, and iteration 0 used kd 0.2. The oval oscillation fell from 0.109 (kd 0.2) to 0.074 (kd 0.4). The cited comparison therefore misstates the record and points the other way. Iteration 2 vs iteration 3 changes only ki, so the kd conclusion should rest on the correct comparison, and the rationale should say the kd evidence is confounded with sensor and speed changes.

3) The speed rejection depends on a confounded comparison. It says iteration 0 at 1.8 gave more oval progress than iteration 1 at 1.5. Those runs also differ in sensor span (x plus or minus 0.04 versus plus or minus 0.06), footprint and kd, so the speed effect is not isolated.

4) 'Oval finish at 1.88 s shows speed is not the constraint' generalises from one finish. Mean progress is 0.45 and the oval mean finish is not defined, so this claim should be labelled as uncertain.

5) The decision rule 'if progress stays flat, test base_speed 1.8 alone' is coherent, but it is set before any new data on this exact design, and the rationale does not say what result on this resubmission would trigger it. Since the race will reproduce iteration 2, the rule would fire on information the team already has.

6) The rationale calls this 'the best-evidenced candidate', which is accurate for score, but it does not state that the resubmission is a score-preserving choice rather than a learning test. The team should decide explicitly which of those two goals this iteration serves.
